title: HE LIFTED HIS HANDS AND BLESSED THEM

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Aaron lifted his hands towards the people and blessed them. And having sacrificed the sin offering, the burnt offering and the fellowship offering, he stepped down." - Lev 9:22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After all the blood and fire, Aaron lifts his hands and blesses the people.

That is what the sacrifices were for. Not to appease an angry deity, but to clear the way for blessing. The offerings ended with a priest raising his hands over a forgiven nation.

The blessing he spoke was almost certainly the one God gave in Numbers: The LORD bless you and keep you; the LORD make his face shine on you and be gracious to you; the LORD turn his face towards you and give you peace (Num 6:24-26).

Now hold that image beside another one. At the end of Luke's Gospel, Jesus led his disciples out to the vicinity of Bethany, and lifting up his hands, he blessed them. While he was blessing them, he left them and was taken up into heaven (Lk 24:50-51).

The last thing the disciples saw of Jesus was His hands raised in blessing. Hands with wounds in them.

Aaron stepped down from the altar. Christ ascended. And His hands have never come down.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I think of God as primarily blessing me or primarily assessing me?
2. What would change today if I pictured Christ's hands raised over my life?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that the sacrifice ends in blessing. Thank You that Christ's hands are lifted over me still. Amen.
